Built to the format, not to my taste

It runs a full-bleed photo off someone's phone with a stroked caption on top, a ranked countdown, and at least one slide that is nothing but the app's own screen. Everything I made before this looked like a magazine ad — which reads as an ad, and gets scrolled.

Mascot — the same campaign, a different renderer

When an agency supplies a mascot and wants a character-led set, nothing about the campaign changes. Same JSON, same ranked array, same copy, same required mention — only the drawing differs. A mascot is also the one character problem that is easy: it is one asset reused on every frame, so nothing has to stay consistent across generations. It matted at 0.023 translucency against a 0.06 limit, where the photographic faces earlier failed between 0.20 and 0.97.

The campaign is data, not copy in a file

A realistic brief: payout terms, platform list, review window, required mention, banned claims, and which assets the agency supplies versus which the clipper brings. Both renderers read this same file.

campaigns/apex-strength.json

payout        $1.00 per 1,000 views · $1 min · $500 max
platforms     instagram, tiktok, youtube, x
review        9 days · budget $7,340 of $12,000 left
requires      9:16 · 5-10 slides · @apex.strength
              must_show_app: true
banned        guaranteed, guaranteed results, lose 10kg in a week, steroid, medically proven, cures
supplied      palette, app screens        (clipper brings the footage)

What broke on the way

  • Every caption refused to fitPoppins' ascender plus descender is about 1.4em, so the flat line-collision check rejected every size at the 1.14 leading these captions want. The block just reported "does not fit". Switched to measured leading, which lifts spacing only as far as the actual ink needs.
  • My own stroke guardThe fitter maximised the type to exactly the box width, then I added the stroke and threw on a 3px overrun. Reserving the stroke before fitting is the fix — and the reservation depends on the size, which depends on the reservation, so it iterates until it settles.
  • Caption across a data rowI hardcoded the app slide's caption at y=1180 and it landed straight on "Overhead press". Now the same band solver places it, and the screen carries three lifts instead of four so there is a real gap to sit in.
  • Speech bubble clipping its own textThe bubble was clamped to a max width while the type stayed at a fixed size, so the longest line ran out through the side. Fit the type first, then size the bubble from what fitted.
  • Subline on a faceSearching for the quietest band independently floated the hook's subline down onto the model. It belongs directly under the title, which is what the reference does.
